title: Sturtian snowball Earth glaciation
summary: The Sturtian glaciation began about 717 million years ago, a date set from volcanic rocks of the Mt. Harper Volcanic Complex in the Ogilvie Mountains, Yukon. The Franklin large igneous province of northern North America was emplaced roughly 0.9 to 1.6 million years earlier, and a Re-Os date on postglacial rocks suggests the glacial epoch lasted about 55 million years.

uncertainty.note: Onset is given as between 717.4 +/-0.2 and 716.9 +/-0.4 Ma (Pu et al.); the end is a postglacial Re-Os date of 662.4 +/-3.9 Ma (Rooney et al.). Start uncertainty is widened to cover the 717.4-716.9 span.

where.modern_name: Ogilvie Mountains, Yukon, Canada (Mt. Harper Volcanic Complex dates the onset; the glaciation was global)
where.historical_name: Margin of Laurentia, low latitude (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: PALEOMAP via GPlates Web Service (MERDITH2021 returns no reconstruction for this point)
paleo.note: Point -138.25, 64.62 reconstructed to 717 Ma; MERDITH2021 returned 999.99 (no plate).

importance.justification: The first of the Cryogenian snowball Earth glaciations, with ice reaching low latitudes.
